title: E.V.O.: Search for Eden
subtitle: A creature of your own
summary: E.V.O.: Search for Eden is an action role-playing game in which the character’s body becomes the main form of equipment. Beginning as a fish, the player travels through a fantastic interpretation of Earth’s prehistoric ages under the guidance of Gaia. The journey moves across five periods, opening different possibilities for the creature’s form. Almanic combines side-scrolling movement and combat with the pleasure of visible transformation, allowing the player to build an increasingly unusual animal while pursuing the promise of Eden.
body: E.V.O.: Search for Eden is an action role-playing game in which the character’s body becomes the main form of equipment. Beginning as a fish, the player travels through a fantastic interpretation of Earth’s prehistoric ages under the guidance of Gaia. The journey moves across five periods, opening different possibilities for the creature’s form. Almanic combines side-scrolling movement and combat with the pleasure of visible transformation, allowing the player to build an increasingly unusual animal while pursuing the promise of Eden.

Defeated creatures leave food that supplies evolution points. Those points can be spent on particular body parts, changing both appearance and abilities. An altered jaw improves one kind of attack; changes to the body can affect movement, jumping or resilience. Progress therefore appears directly on the creature rather than being confined to a numerical increase. The player decides which immediate weakness to address and which new form to try, with the available choices changing as the adventure reaches another stage of its fictional natural history.

Each period has a map of individual stages populated by different organisms. Biting, ramming or jumping can provide ways to deal with them, while avoiding a creature may preserve health. Food, plants and selected transformations offer recovery, connecting survival with the evolution system. Crystals add guidance, points or temporary bodies that let the player experience another form. E.V.O. takes broad liberties with history, but its design makes a clear invitation: experiment with the body, then discover what that body allows in the surrounding world.
